title: Web Browser MCP
tagline: A tool that lets AI agents like Claude use a real Chrome browser
summary: I built a tool that lets Claude Code and other AI agents control a real Chrome browser on my computer, instead of just downloading raw web pages. It keeps logins between runs, shows the AI numbered boxes over everything it can click, and lets me watch what it's doing live.

overview.what: A tool that lets Claude Code and other AI agents use a real Chrome browser on my computer, instead of just downloading raw web pages.
overview.why: A lot of my automation projects kept needing the same thing: a browser that could handle modern websites and stay signed in. I kept rebuilding it, so I made it its own project.
overview.did: I built a small server that runs Chrome, and an MCP layer on top with tools like navigate, snapshot, click and type, plus numbered boxes over everything clickable and a live viewer.
overview.result: Claude and my scripts can share one signed-in browser, and the live viewer makes it easy to see why an agent is stuck. I only use it on sites and accounts where that's allowed.

hero.alt: Web Browser MCP cover showing a browser window beside a snapshot, act, and verify tool loop

sections.heading: How the AI sees a page
body: The most useful part is the snapshot. It finds everything on the page you can click or type into, gives each one a number, and draws numbered boxes on a screenshot. The AI gets both the picture and the list, so it can say "click 12" instead of guessing where to click. Then it looks at the page again to make sure it worked.

media.alt: Four-step agent interaction loop showing snapshot, reason, act, and verify followed by waiting for a settled page
media.caption: Snapshot, decide, act, check.

sections.heading: How it's put together
body: There are two layers. The bottom one is a small server that runs Chrome and keeps track of profiles and tabs. The top one is an MCP server, which is the standard way to give Claude new tools, with tools like navigate, snapshot, click and type.
Chrome only lets one program use a profile at a time, so splitting it this way lets my scripts and Claude share the same signed-in browser instead of fighting over it.

media.alt: Architecture diagram connecting Claude Code through FastMCP and FastAPI to a browser engine with profiles, actions, capture, and live observability
media.caption: Claude talks to the MCP layer, which talks to the server that runs Chrome.

sections.heading: Watching it work
body: Every action gets logged with how long it took and whether it worked. Anything typed only shows up as its length, so passwords never end up in the log. There's also a live viewer that shows the browser next to the action log, which made it way easier to see why an agent was stuck.

sections.heading: What's next
body: It runs on my own computer, and I only use it on sites and accounts where that's allowed. Next I want to record a short demo of Claude filling out a test form while the live viewer shows every step.
